correctness.rationale: The density follows from an exact decomposition into 3 same-path ordered square areas and 3 two-path ordered cross areas. The four possible pole routes yield precisely the polygon inequalities in RESULT.md. Same-path tails give nonzero derivative jumps only at (u+m)/2 for u>m; cross tails only where the x+y-strip collapses at (u+v)/2, with first-order area 2 min(u,v,w) epsilon. All other polygon combinatorial events alter area by O(epsilon²). Sum coefficients are strictly negative, so ties cannot cancel. The formula f(0+)=2/L and explicit 1-,2-,3-jump inverse determine all a,b,c. Exact-arithmetic and independent simulation checks passed. Finite tests are not relied on for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The natural theta graph is the smallest edge-sharing two-cycle network beyond cactus graphs. A global scalar point-pair distance law generally obscures spatial labels, yet here it determines all edge lengths even on symmetric boundaries. The screened longest-cycle coefficient is structurally distinct from the cactus coefficient and demonstrates a specific noncactus mechanism relevant to quantitative inverse problems. It is a complete, motivated family classification rather than an arbitrary numerical example.
